### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b32dc22272e606389d93f0ec98294c47771745a8` — the merge of head `866523ae733c6337d578bb4847516261affd821b` into base `2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b32dc22272e606389d93f0ec98294c47771745a8 && git checkout b32dc22272e606389d93f0ec98294c47771745a8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12 866523ae733c6337d578bb4847516261affd821b && git checkout -B drift-repro 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12 && git merge --no-ff 866523ae733c6337d578bb4847516261affd821b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0b8ad7e7dc7f8fb2d89e9db70f508796fc1213e3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/field.json, content/docs/references/data/field.mdx, content/docs/references/data/object.mdx, content/docs/references/system/migration.mdx, .changeset/34197-lookup-record-reference.md, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/lookupRecordReference.ts, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/RecordPickerDialog.tsx, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/PeoplePicker.tsx, ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-form/src/sectionFields.ts, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.recordReference-34197.test.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/lookupRecordHop-34197.test.tsx, ui/examples/schema-catalog/test/form-field-channel-census-12130.test.tsx

Read at 2026-11-16T04:37Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6907355140; lane request 6907342354 on mailbox #33873. Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:ui#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Read against merge base `43dd5656` (16 files, +907/−63). Every path of the diff was read; code outside the diff was read, not reviewed. Mechanisms behind the security-adjacent findings are in the seat's private notes, not here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Describes-only holds.** `field.zod.ts` changes four describe strings and one docblock sentence. No key, type, refinement or regex moves; `LOOKUP_FILTER_RECORD_PATH_RE`, `refuseMalformedLookupFilterEntry` and the `strictObject` row are untouched. The accept set at head equals the accept set at the base.
- **Generated references match source.** `data/field.mdx`, `data/object.mdx` and `system/migration.mdx` carry the new `lookupFilters`, `value` and `orEmpty` sentences verbatim; no `[PLANNED — not enforced]` picker sentence and no "filter panel" remain in the three pages or in `field.zod.ts`.
- **`orEmpty` on the wire matches the spec's filter contract.** `lookupFiltersToRecord` sends the comparison OR a `$null: true` match on the same column, one member of a `$and` list, only for the six operators the spec pairs the flag with. `filter.zod.ts` declares `$null` and the `$or` spelling; the repo's one client lowering (`ui/packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts`) lowers `$and` / `$or` groups beside field keys and `$null` by its flag. None of the three consumers (popover, table picker, people picker) writes a second `$and` that the spread could overwrite. Bound: read, not run end to end against a server.
- **The stamp reaches the reader only from the two builders.** `withRecordBeingEdited` has two callers, `ObjectForm` (auto layout) and `fromObjectSchema` in `sectionFields.ts`; the latter feeds Modal, Drawer, Tabbed and Wizard forms and `buildFlatFields` (Modal and Drawer). Each edits or creates one record. Object-field metadata and action-parameter documents are closed shapes that refuse the key, and the two dialogs that hand the widget sibling parameters build its field from enumerated keys. See S2 for the bound on that statement.
- **The one-hop read runs as the signed-in user,** through the widget's own data source, selecting the hop fields alone. Nothing the user's session cannot read enters the query. See S1 for what happens when the read returns nothing.
- **N6 (from records 6901257122 / 6903625797 on PR #34078): closed.** Both the describe and the `LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema` docblock now name "a bulk action over selected rows"; `ui/packages/plugin-list/src` has no `lookupFilters` read at head, so removing "a filter panel" is the correct direction.
- **N8 (same records): unchanged, by design.** `orEmpty: false` is sent as a plain comparison; the spec's refusal of the flag outside the six is untouched.
- **Liveness.** The `lookupFilters` row stays `live`; the new citations use the in-repo `ui/packages/…#symbol` spelling the checker prescribes. The row's note is narrative the checker does not scan. `Spec property liveness` is green on this head.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` is correct: prose only, no accept-set change. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are correct on both the PR body and the changeset, and the two agree. `patch` on `@object-ui/fields` (two new exports, a widened prop type that every previous caller still satisfies) and `@object-ui/plugin-form` is the lane seat's accept; nothing read here contradicts it.

CI on this head at read time: 69 check-runs, 27 success, 11 skipped, 31 in progress, 0 failed. Green so far include Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Lint & Repo Gates, Build Docs and Governed Surface Queue Guard. Still running: Test UI (16 shards), Test Core (8 shards), Type Check UI, Type Check workspace and consumer gates, Lint UI, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. This verdict does not depend on them.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Authorization-adjacent.** A lookup filter narrows which records a user may pick. The spec states the picker narrows the choice only and that a rule the save must enforce belongs on the server. Every unresolved case at head fails open (the entry is left out, the list is wider). That is the ruled direction (6900252552 §1) for an empty value and for a host with no record; M1 and S1 are the cases where it happens outside what the contract says.
- **Server refusal is unmeasured (S3).** The describe and the ledger note both say an unresolved `{ $record }` reaching a server is refused. No server path names the comparand at head and the PR measured nothing live.
- **Hand-written docs** (`content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`, `relationships.mdx`) do not teach `{ $record }` or `orEmpty`; the Skills-docs follow-up carries it. Not a finding on this PR.
- **Ablations A1 to A12 are the dev's readings,** not re-run here (read-only). By reading, the unstamped pin and its stamped control differ only in the stamp and assert different queries, and the two form pins go through the real `ObjectForm` and `ModalForm`.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` against its first consumer.**

M1 (must-fix) — The describes now promise resolution on surfaces where the picker drops the entry. With the `[PLANNED — not enforced]` markers gone, the `lookupFilters` describe reads "the picker sends that value in its place", the `value` describe reads "The picker sends the referenced value in place of the reference", and the only exceptions named are an empty value and "a picker with no single record being edited (a bulk action over selected rows)". At head the picker resolves only on a field a record form stamped. Detail-page inline edit, the header highlight, related-list inline edit and the single-record action dialog each edit exactly one record, hand the widget that record, and leave every `{ $record }` entry out. The PR body says so in its Acceptance notes, the changeset says "Record forms opt in … Any other host … leaves every `{ $record }` entry out", and the ledger note says the same; the published describe, the docblock's "An empty value" rule and the three generated pages do not. An author reading the reference will expect the filter on inline edit and get a wider candidate list than they wrote, with no signal. Ruling 6900252552 §1 covers a host with no single record; these hosts have one. Either remedy clears it: (a) say it in the contract — the `lookupFilters` and `value` describes and the docblock name where the reference resolves (record forms: the auto layout, modal, drawer, tabbed, wizard) and that every other picker host, inline edit on a record page included, leaves the entry out, then regenerate; or (b) opt those hosts in with `withRecordBeingEdited` and a pin each, so the sentence as written becomes true. (a) is describes-only and keeps this PR's shape.

S1 (should-fix) — A hop whose value cannot be read is treated as empty, and the contract lists only empty values. The docblock and describe enumerate null, unset, an empty string and an unset hop lookup. The resolver also leaves the entry out when the hop row or its field does not come back, when the host names no object for the hop, and when the host has no single-row reader. The dev-mode warning covers two of those and none of them in production. Add the case to the describe's empty-value sentence ("or cannot be read"), and consider saying something once when a read fails.

S2 (should-fix) — "Runtime-only" is held by the authoring validators and by convention, not pinned at the hosts it protects. The census ledgers the key correctly and I found no document shape that carries it to a host without a record. But the pin for the unstamped side renders `LookupField` directly with hand-built values; no pin goes through the real bulk action dialog or the action parameter dialog, and no pin shows that a document which writes the key gains nothing. One pin through each real dialog (a parameter whose `lookupFilters` read `{ $record }` and a same-named sibling parameter, asserting the entry is left out) would hold the invariant r1 was made for.

S3 (should-fix, a follow-up card is acceptable) — The sentence "A { $record } that reaches a server unresolved is refused, never read as null" now stands in a describe with no PLANNED marker beside it, and in the ledger note this PR rewrote, while the refusal is unmeasured for either position a reference can take in a filter. Measure it (one server-side pin per position) or file the carrier card and cite it from the ledger note.

N1 (nit) — `liveness/field.json`: the `lookupFilters` note was re-read and rewritten for this PR but `verifiedAt` still reads 2026-10-16.

N2 (nit) — `LookupField.tsx`: the `NO_EDITED_RECORD` constant sits between two import statements.

**Implementing files.** Apart from M1 and S1, the code agrees with the contract it implements: the path grammar read is the spec's (a field, or one hop); an expanded related row collapses to its id; the query keys on the resolved values, so a referenced field re-queries and an unrelated one does not; candidate queries and both Level-2 pickers are held while a hop read is pending; `lookupFiltersToRecord` drops any entry still carrying a reference, so none reaches the wire from this client; literal entries and `dependsOn` pass through as the authored array.

Prior ids: none on this PR (first review). Carried from PR #34078: N6 closed, N8 unchanged by design.
